findings.claim: The new verification doctrine removes every behavioral gate for the ordinary Dart graph/Riverpod surface, so the next package release of the non-DevTools entry would ship on static checks alone.
findings.evidence: The hunk deletes `pnpm run dart:test`, `pnpm run test:dart-graph-riverpod`, and `pnpm run bdd:dart-graph-riverpod` from the release boundary, states "Do not run or cite the legacy unit, widget, provider, golden, Node, Cucumber, or partial suites", and declares "Historical Flutter unit/widget/golden receipts remain audit history ... not current completion or release evidence" — while the only assembled acceptance flow named (`verify:devtools-flutter-controller`) exercises the optional DevTools controller, not the ordinary library. No replacement behavioral flow for the ordinary surface is introduced anywhere in the diff (RELEASING.md hunk shows the same removal).
findings.suggested_fix: Either keep one assembled acceptance flow that covers the ordinary graph/Riverpod surface as release evidence, or state explicitly which future gate restores behavioral coverage for the non-DevTools entry before the next pub.dev release.

findings.claim: verification.md's refiner claims are stale and internally contradicted by the refiner state files shipped in the same diff.
findings.evidence: verification.md says "Artifact-refiner iteration 2 passed all six blocking constraints and was finalized after the first adversarial-review correction round", but `.refiner/artifacts/.../state.json` records `current_iteration: 3` with `finalized_at: "2026-08-30T02:41:02Z"`, and `refinement_log.md` iteration 3 says convergence is only "terminate after the corrected artifact passes fresh isolated review and strict sycophancy screening". Simultaneously, `state.json` is marked finalized while verification.md itself says "Final archive remains contingent on a fresh isolated review" — i.e., the refiner artifact declares itself finalized before the gate its own log says is still pending.
findings.suggested_fix: Update verification.md to describe iteration 3, and either clear `finalized_at`/`convergence_status` in state.json until the fresh review passes or reconcile the log's termination condition with the recorded finalization.

findings.claim: The declaration collector silently drops public declarations with nullable function-typed returns (`Function()?`) or function types with nested function-typed parameters, and because the same collector backs both `--write` and verify, the ledger round-trips cleanly while missing real public API (fail-open).
findings.evidence: The new hunk parses with `/^(?:[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_<>,?.]*\s+)?Function\([^)]*\)\s+([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\s*(?:<[^>{;]+>)?\s*\(/` — after `Function(...)` it requires whitespace before the name, so `void Function()? name(` never matches (the `?` breaks it), and `[^)]*` stops at the first `)` so `void Function(void Function()) name(` also never matches; the general `fn` fallback cannot match either because its return-type character class excludes `(` and `?` in that position. A missed declaration is absent from both the expected and actual ledger, so `verifyLedger` passes and the hardcoded 93/99 counts only trip on additions, not on silently skipped declarations already in source.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend the callable-return regex to allow `?` after `Function(...)` and balanced/nested parameter lists, or derive declarations from `dart doc` index.json (already generated in Task 9) instead of regex parsing; add a cross-check that dartdoc public names ⊆ ledger names.

findings.claim: The DevTools publication block hardcodes `publishedArchiveVersion: "3.0.1"` and `publishedArchiveIncludesLibrary: false` in the generator while `version` is read dynamically from the pubspec, so the script's output becomes a false statement the moment a version containing `devtools.dart` is published.
findings.evidence: In `expectedDartDevtoolsLedger()`: `publication: { status: "repository-source-only", publishedArchiveVersion: "3.0.1", publishedArchiveIncludesLibrary: false }` is a literal, whereas the root ledger's `version` comes from `pubspec.yaml`. The fail-closed string comparison forces a regeneration at the next version bump, but regeneration will emit this same stale block unless a human remembers to edit the script.
findings.suggested_fix: Read the published-archive status from a checked-in data file (e.g., `release/pubdev-registry-status.json`, which exists in the file tree) or add a code comment plus a release-checklist step that flips this block at publication time.
